holidays.name: National Card Playing Day
holidays.description: A day to shuffle up and deal. Dust off the deck and play poker, rummy, solitaire, or go fish with friends and family.
holidays.origin: Unofficial observance listed in national day calendars, tied to the lull between Christmas and New Year's, when families are gathered and looking for indoor entertainment.
holidays.funFact: A standard 52-card deck is often said to mirror the calendar: 52 cards for the weeks in a year, 4 suits for the seasons, and 13 cards per suit for the lunar cycles in a season.

holidays.name: Holy Innocents' Day (Childermas)
holidays.description: A Christian feast day remembering the infants killed by King Herod. In some traditions it was considered so unlucky that people avoided starting new projects.
holidays.origin: Observed since at least the 5th century and rooted in the Gospel of Matthew. In medieval Europe it included the quirky tradition of the Boy Bishop, where a choirboy was appointed to lead church services.
holidays.funFact: In Spain and Latin America, December 28 is the Día de los Santos Inocentes, which is basically April Fools' Day, complete with pranks and fake news stories in newspapers.

holidays.name: Tick Tock Day
holidays.description: A day to think about time, clocks, and the passing of the last days of the year. Set your clocks right and wonder where the year went.
holidays.origin: A modern unofficial observance that plays on the countdown to New Year's Eve, just a few days away.
holidays.funFact: Clocks have been tick-tocking for centuries, but the pendulum clock, invented by Christiaan Huygens in 1656, made accurate timekeeping possible for the first time.

holidays.name: National Short Film Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the shortest night of the year in the Northern Hemisphere's film world, spotlighting movies that tell a complete story in a handful of minutes.
holidays.origin: Created by the short film community and observed on or around December 21 internationally. The date was chosen because the winter solstice is the shortest day of the year, so it only appears here as a movie lover's extra celebration. It is often paired with the date of the first public commercial film screening.
holidays.funFact: The first commercial movie screening by the Lumière brothers took place on December 28, 1895, in Paris, and the films were each only about 50 seconds long.

holidays.name: Pledge of Allegiance Day
holidays.description: A day recognizing the U.S. Pledge of Allegiance, which was formally recognized by Congress in 1942.
holidays.origin: President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed the bill on December 28, 1942, officially adopting the Pledge as part of the U.S. Flag Code.
holidays.funFact: The original Pledge, written in 1892, did not include the words 'under God.' Those were added in 1954, and the original version also had a different gesture accompanying it.
